question: Drugs causing hypokalemia are : a) Amphotericin B b) Insulin c) Cyclosporine d) Carbenoxolone e) NSAIDs
analysis: Amphotericin B is known to cause hypokalemia due to its effects on renal potassium handling. Insulin can also lead to hypokalemia by driving potassium into cells. Cyclosporine and NSAIDs are not typically associated with hypokalemia, while carbenoxolone can cause hypokalemia as well. Therefore, the drugs causing hypokalemia are Amphotericin B, Insulin, and Carbenoxolone, which corresponds to option 'acd'.
